description: The bar chart, titled "The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets," illustrates the distribution of hate speech targets across different years from 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the years, ranging from 2012 to 2022, while the vertical axis indicates the proportion of targets, scaled from 0.0 to 1.0. Each vertical bar corresponds to a specific year and is segmented into colored portions, representing the proportion of hate speech directed at different target groups. The legend on the right identifies five target categories: "0" (blue), "1" (orange), "2-4" (green), "5-7" (red), and "8+" (purple). The data reveals that in 2012 and 2013, the majority of hate speech was directed at a single target (blue segment). From 2014 to 2016, the distribution shifted, with a significant portion of hate speech targeting groups of 2-4 individuals (green segment). The proportion of hate speech targeting a single target (blue segment) remained high in 2017 and 2018, but the proportion targeting groups of 2-4 individuals (green segment) decreased. In 2019, the proportion of hate speech targeting a single target (blue segment) decreased, while the proportion targeting groups of 5-7 individuals (red segment) increased. The proportion of hate speech targeting a single target (blue segment) continued to decrease in 2020 and 2021, while the proportion targeting groups of 5-7 individuals (red segment) increased. In 2022, the proportion of hate speech targeting a single target (blue segment) was the lowest, while the proportion targeting groups of 5-7 individuals (red segment) was the highest. The chart also shows that the proportion of hate speech targeting groups of 8+ individuals (purple segment) was relatively low in all years.
